BIST STOCK DAILY BRIEF | November 08, 2026

MARKET OVERVIEW

1. What is the Current Market Regime?
RISK-ON: normal volatility at 32.1% and strong breadth, with 8/8 sectors positive over one week. Broad participation supports risk-taking, though the negative one-month returns across several sectors argue for selectivity.

2. Which sectors are leading?
Transportation leads (+21.49% 1W, +5.09% 1M), with THYAO (1W: +23.55% | 1M: +4.54%) ABOVE TREND. Technology & Telecom (+16.89% 1W, +4.12% 1M) is next, led by KONTR (1W: +46.45% | 1M: +29.47%) ABOVE TREND.

3. Which sectors are lagging?
Retail & Food is the relative laggard despite a positive 1W average (+5.62%), with SOKM (1W: -6.58% | 1M: -11.93%) BELOW TREND. Construction & REIT (+6.05% 1W, -10.11% 1M) remains weak on the monthly view; TKFEN (1W: -1.25% | 1M: -29.48%) is BELOW TREND.

STOCK PERFORMANCE

4. Top Performing Stocks?
The five strongest 1W performers are KONTR (1W: +46.45% | 1M: +29.47%) ABOVE TREND, THYAO (1W: +23.55% | 1M: +4.54%) ABOVE TREND, and PGSUS (1W: +23.13% | 1M: +3.74%) ABOVE TREND. Also leading: TRMET (1W: +18.98% | 1M: -11.54%) RECOVERY and TAVHL (1W: +17.80% | 1M: +6.99%) ABOVE TREND.

5. Worst Performing Stocks?
The weakest 1W performers are SOKM (1W: -6.58% | 1M: -11.93%) BELOW TREND, ASELS (1W: -4.39% | 1M: -4.87%) BELOW TREND, and TUPRS (1W: -1.75% | 1M: -11.13%) BELOW TREND. TKFEN (1W: -1.25% | 1M: -29.48%) and TCELL (1W: -0.11% | 1M: -9.46%) are also BELOW TREND.

6. Momentum Stocks?
Near-term momentum is concentrated in transportation and technology: KONTR (1W: +46.45% | 1M: +29.47%) ABOVE TREND, THYAO (1W: +23.55% | 1M: +4.54%) ABOVE TREND, and PGSUS (1W: +23.13% | 1M: +3.74%) ABOVE TREND. The sharp 1W gains in TRMET (1W: +18.98% | 1M: -11.54%) and VESTL (1W: +16.15% | 1M: -25.84%) are RECOVERY moves, not yet monthly confirmations.

SECTOR OUTLOOK

7. Banking Sector Outlook?
Banking breadth is constructive, with the sector up 12.17% over 1W and 1.43% over 1M. GARAN (1W: +15.26% | 1M: +11.09%), ISCTR (1W: +14.08% | 1M: +2.47%) and YKBNK (1W: +9.66% | 1M: +1.75%) are ABOVE TREND; AKBNK (1W: +12.73% | 1M: -0.87%) is in RECOVERY.

8. Industrial Sector Outlook?
Heavy Industry gained 6.65% over 1W but remains down 11.74% over 1M, signaling a short-term rebound against a weak monthly backdrop. TOASO (1W: +15.06% | 1M: -7.43%), FROTO (1W: +11.76% | 1M: -0.95%) and EREGL (1W: +4.72% | 1M: -14.95%) are in RECOVERY, while ASELS (1W: -4.39% | 1M: -4.87%) is BELOW TREND.

9. Energy & Chemicals Outlook?
The sector rose 9.54% over 1W but remains down 13.46% over 1M, making the rebound uneven. TRMET (1W: +18.98% | 1M: -11.54%) and GUBRF (1W: +15.58% | 1M: -26.28%) are in RECOVERY, while TUPRS (1W: -1.75% | 1M: -11.13%) is BELOW TREND.

PORTFOLIO STRATEGY

10. Portfolio Recommendation?
Maintain a measured risk-on stance, favoring leaders with positive 1W and 1M trends while keeping exposure diversified. Treat sharp rebounds with negative 1M performance as tactical until they show stronger follow-through.

NEXT WEEK OUTLOOK

11. Stocks to Watch Next Week?
Monitor KONTR (1W: +46.45% | 1M: +29.47%) ABOVE TREND and GARAN (1W: +15.26% | 1M: +11.09%) ABOVE TREND for continuation. THYAO (1W: +23.55% | 1M: +4.54%) is also ABOVE TREND, while TRMET (1W: +18.98% | 1M: -11.54%) and FROTO (1W: +11.76% | 1M: -0.95%) are RECOVERY candidates where follow-through matters.

12. Sectors to Watch Next Week?
Transportation and Banking & Finance have the strongest combination of 1W and 1M sector returns. Watch Energy & Chemicals for evidence that its strong weekly rebound can reverse the still-weak monthly trend.

13. Key Levels & Triggers?
No XU100 support or resistance levels were supplied, so specific index levels cannot be stated. Key triggers are whether breadth remains broad and whether recent sector and stock rebounds extend into sustained monthly improvement.

EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

Normal volatility and positive breadth across all eight sectors support a RISK-ON stance, with Transportation, Technology & Telecom, and Banking leading. Prefer confirmed ABOVE TREND names; rebounds in weak-monthly sectors remain vulnerable to reversal.
